# Standing instructions

## Delegating to Claude CLI sub-agents

Substantial coding work can be delegated to the `claude-*` sub-agents, which run
the Claude Code CLI as their own autonomous process (their own tools, on the model
named below). Pick by task difficulty, not by guessing a model:

- **claude-fast** (Haiku) — cheap, well-specified, mechanical tasks: renames, small
  localized edits, formatting, simple lookups. No cross-file reasoning.
- **claude-general** (Sonnet) — the default for a self-contained coding task you can
  hand off end-to-end.
- **claude-deep** (Opus) — the hardest tasks: multi-file refactors, architecture and
  design, subtle debugging, anything needing maximum reasoning. Slower and costlier,
  so reserve it for work that genuinely needs it.

Guidance:
- Delegate when a sub-task is self-contained and benefits from a clean, separate
  context; keep orchestration, synthesis, and user-facing decisions yourself.
- Match the agent to the difficulty: don't send a one-line rename to claude-deep, and
  don't send an architecture change to claude-fast.
- A CLI agent only edits files when the session is in `auto` mode; in `ask`/`plan` it
  runs read-only. It runs under the Claude CLI's own auth/permissions — it does not
  inherit this harness's MCP grants or tool-approval hooks.
- These run on a separate (Claude) account and bill independently of this harness's
  own model.
